subject: Packaging options for trace retention vs archival credits
messages:
From: Asha Malik <asha@logix.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logix Procurement <procurement@logix.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying bundle economics for trace vs archival credits

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team found the live trace playback and span-level filtering compelling. Procurement asked me to follow up with a clear ask: we currently have two consumption patterns that map to different budgets — (1) hot/live trace retention for debugging (short window, high QPS) and (2) long-term archival for compliance and analytics.

Before we move to an internal approval, can Redwood propose (a) a pricing comparison between buying credits for archival storage vs buying a live-trace retention add-on, and (b) a volume discount path if we commit for 12 months across both?

Key constraints:
- We need ~30TB/month archived ingest (cold) with 24-month retention.
- Live trace retention would be for a 30-day hot window at ~400 QPS peak; most spikes are concentrated in a small subset of services.
- Security: SOC2 and VPC peering in place.

Could you outline practical bundling options (e.g., blended credits, seat/ingest splits, or hybrid commit) and any carrier discounts or pilot concessions you typically make for mid-market healthcare customers? We have a procurement cadence next Tuesday and would like to show 1–2 concrete proposals.

Appreciate it —
Asha
Principal SRE, Logix Health
A: +1 415 555 0124

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Malik <asha@logix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying bundle economics for trace vs archival credits

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear constraints. Looping in Ben (price/packaging) and Kimberly (commercial/legal) so we can put together a short set of concrete options ahead of your procurement meeting.

High-level thoughts (quick):
- Archival credits are more cost-effective for pure long-term storage; they amortize on ingest TB and have cheaper per-GB/month pricing once committed.
- Live-trace retention (the "hot" add-on) is priced to cover read/ingest QPS for replay and UI costs; it's more expensive per-GB but preserves low-latency UX for engineers.

Proposed deliverables by EOD Monday:
1) Two pricing sheets: (A) Archival-first (bulk credits + optional 30-day hot window as a crossover SKU) and (B) Hot-first (primary live-trace capacity + archival credits for overflow).
2) A 3-tier volume discount ladder for a 12-month commit (starting at 10% for base commit, 18% at mid, 25% at large).
3) A small pilot concession (1 month of hot window waived or a credit) to help Logix validate the hot-path cost.

Ben, Kimberly — can you turn this into a short commercial note with attachments (SKU sheet, MAP) and a recommended walk-away concession that preserves our margin? Asha — would you prefer the numbers as monthly ARR-style amortized pricing or a table of per-unit costs?

Thanks,
Connor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Malik <asha@logix.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying bundle economics for trace vs archival credits

Asha — attaching a concise SKU export and a minimal actionable commercial proposal. See attachment: trace-retention-sku_v2.xlsx and a short MAP (attached PDF). Highlights below:

Option A — Archival-first (recommended if long-term cost pressure):
- Commit: 360TB ingest/year (30TB/mo) archival credits
- Price: $0.012/GB-month (post-commit) => blended archival rate
- Hot add-on: 30-day live window as a burstable SKU priced at $X per peak QPS with 10% discount at commit
- 12-month commit discount ladder: 10% @ baseline (360TB), 16% @ +25% commit, 22% @ +50% commit

Option B — Live-first (recommended if debugging velocity is highest):
- Commit: baseline live capacity for 400 QPS with an on-demand archival supplement
- Price: tailored per-QPS with an included 14 days of hot retention; archival credits billed monthly with 12% discount on commit

Concession proposal (pilot):
- Pilot: 60 days of waived live-window charges for primary services (up to 100 QPS sustained) + $15k migration credit to offset initial archive ingest cost.

Attached files: trace-retention-sku_v2.xlsx (pricing matrix), MAP-Logix-2026.pdf (commercial terms).

Let me know if you want the numbers as a single blended monthly figure — happy to convert. If Logix can share a 12-month commit intent by EOW we can lock the 16% tier.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[attachment: trace-retention-sku_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[attachment: MAP-Logix-2026.pdf (proposal PDF)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Malik <asha@logix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2026 15:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying bundle economics for trace vs archival credits

Asha — quick commercial position from Redwood (high level):

1) We think Option A (archival-first with a burstable hot add-on) typically yields the best TCO for compliance-heavy customers like Logix. The numbers Ben provided are aligned with comparable deals in healthcare.

2) To address procurement checkpoints:
- We can include a 30-day SLA credit and standard SOC2 artifacts in the contract.
- For the 12-month commit ladder, we can formalize the 16% mid-tier at a signed SOW / order form by 2026-11-30.

3) Pilot concession (final):
- 45 days of waived live-window charges (up to 100 QPS) + $12,500 archival ingest credit applied against first monthly invoice.
- If Logix signs the order form within 14 days after pilot completion, we will honor the 16% discount tier retroactively to pilot start.

Next steps:
- Asha: confirm whether procurement prefers (i) blended monthly ARR line item or (ii) separate line items for live and archival for internal chargeback.
- Connor/Ben: I'll prepare a one-page SOW and an edited MAP to reflect the 45-day/cap concession and the retroactive discount path.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow if useful.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
